title: Unsafe Deserialization via ObjectInputStream
platform_conditions: Java SE 8+ standard library; applies wherever Java serialization endpoints exist (servlet apps, RMI, JMS), independent of OS
security_mechanism: ObjectInputStream.readObject reads the class descriptor named in the stream, loads that class through the classloader, instantiates it WITHOUT running its normal constructors, and invokes its readObject/defaultReadObject/readResolve hooks. An attacker who controls the stream therefore only needs a gadget class present on the classpath whose deserialization hooks (or subsequent toString/compare/equals invocations) chain into Runtime.exec or template/EL evaluation — the deserializer executes the attacker's chosen code path itself. XMLDecoder performs an analogous reconstruction from XML expression documents, and JSON/YAML binders with polymorphic type metadata (a @class/@type property) reach the same instantiation-through-input shape.

source_sink_clues.source: Serialized payloads an attacker can write: HTTP cookies/parameters, RMI or JMS endpoints, session stores, uploaded files, queue messages.
source_sink_clues.sink: ObjectInputStream.readObject / readUnshared on attacker-influenced streams; XMLDecoder.readObject; JSON/YAML deserializers configured with polymorphic type resolution from the payload

tracking_guards: Check for a look-ahead deserialization filter: JEP 290 ObjectInputFilter (or a library like a validating ObjectInputStream) with a class allowlist applied BEFORE instantiation, or replacement by a data-only format (JSON into fixed types). Note that filters must reject by default (ALLOWLIST), and a blacklist is not a guard.
not_candidate_when: The stream is produced and consumed inside one trust domain with no network or shared-storage exposure, an ObjectInputFilter with an explicit class allowlist is installed on the stream, or the payload is covered by an integrity check (HMAC/signature) verified before deserialization with a key the attacker cannot read.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(is); Object obj = ois.readObject();
public_references: Oracle: Secure Coding Guidelines for Java SE, Object Deserialization section — https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/seccodeguide.html
